sentenceSets.sentence: She had grown bored with the humdrum routine and sought out assignments that required something unpredictable of her.

answerChoices.reasoning: A demanding routine would tax her, but she is leaving in search of unpredictability, which suggests the old work was the same every day rather than too hard.
Grueling work exhausts, and exhaustion would send someone toward easier duties rather than toward assignments that keep her guessing.
Solitude would make company the remedy, yet what she seeks is work whose demands cannot be anticipated.
Chaos is already unpredictable, which would give her no reason to go looking for the unpredictable elsewhere.
Good pay is not the sort of quality that produces boredom or drives someone toward less certain work.
Prestige concerns how others regard the job and does not explain the tedium she is escaping.
A temporary routine would end on its own, making her search for new assignments unnecessary.
Working with others is a feature of how the job is organized, not a source of the sameness she has tired of.
Exhilaration would be what she is seeking, not what she has grown bored with.
Variety is the quality her new assignments promise, so it cannot describe the routine she left.
Danger is the opposite of a routine dull enough to send her looking for surprises.

sentenceSets.sentence: Most of the diary is humdrum, full of laundry lists and weather notes, and then on one page the war arrives.

answerChoices.reasoning: Cryptic entries would be hard to decipher, but laundry lists and weather notes are perfectly clear and simply uneventful.
Fragmentary writing would leave gaps, whereas the diary is described as full of small daily particulars.
Sentimentality would show feeling on the page, while the examples given are inventories and observations of the weather.
Meticulousness would praise the diarist's care, but the contrast with the war's arrival rests on how unremarkable the earlier pages are.
If the entries could not be read, no one could tell that they concerned laundry and weather.
Missing dates would be a problem of chronology, not of how ordinary the contents are.
An encoded diary would conceal its contents, which are plainly visible here.
Nothing can be written after the diarist's death, and the point being made concerns the character of the entries.
Harrowing material is what arrives on the one page, in contrast with everything before it.
Momentousness belongs to the war's arrival, which the sentence sets against the rest of the diary.
A riveting account would not need the turn the sentence introduces with the word 'then'.

sentenceSets.sentence: What sounds humdrum on paper turns out to be the most consequential job in the building: approving every purchase order.

answerChoices.reasoning: Menial work is lowly and physical, but the job turns out to be the most consequential in the building, which makes the mismatch one of apparent dullness rather than low status.
Obscurity would mean few people know the job exists, whereas the sentence contrasts how it reads in a description with what it actually controls.
A technical job would sound difficult rather than unremarkable, which is the impression the sentence says the description gives.
A temporary post would sound short-lived, not dull, and duration plays no part in the surprise the sentence delivers.
Compensation is never mentioned, and the reversal turns on the authority the role carries.
Danger would make the job sound dramatic on paper, undercutting the contrast being drawn.
Seasonality concerns when the work happens, not how unexciting it appears in writing.
Working remotely is a matter of location, and this role is explicitly situated in the building.
If the job sounded glamorous on paper there would be nothing surprising about its importance.
A thrilling description would spoil the reversal the sentence builds toward.
A coveted post is one everyone already wants, which removes the surprise about its real power.
